findings.text: the published claim's pre-spawn shape — no pid, so a reader sees a run whose process has not started rather than a pid that may be the composer's — is stated as load-bearing by the writer's docstring (dispatch.py:1095-1097) and held by no assertion: measured, wrapping `_publish_launch_claim` so the claim carries the live pid of the composing process leaves all four cases green (logs/review-claim-shape-probe.log, 4 passed), while the reason a claims reader reports changes from "records no worker process yet" (claims.py:250-255) to "its worker is still running as pid N" and, once that process ends, to the death claim the shape exists to avoid; the case that holds the claim in flight (test 2) is where one assertion on the record's keys and phase would pin it.

item_verdicts.diff: a7413c1d adds the identity exclusion to the claims read (dispatch.py:991), the publication helper and its call before the worktree step (dispatch.py:1069, :3938), the identity-excluded re-check at the pointer write (:4241-:4246), and the unwind that releases the claim on a later refusal; 3704ed56 adds the plan section, the evidence anchor and the figure. The re-check is what makes the exclusion worth having: two dispatches can both clear the admission read before either publishes (dispatch.py:3620), and because each publishes before it re-reads, a mutual miss is impossible and the second arriver is the one refused.
item_verdicts.done_when: the node's gate is one invocation over the ten named files: 84 passed, exit 0 at head and 82 passed, 2 failed, exit 1 in the base scratch tree, the two reds being exactly the added seam assertions; I re-derived the added module's arms myself in pinned scratch trees with the imported package and dispatch modules asserted inside each tree — head 3704ed56 4 passed, base 3be868de 2 failed 2 passed — so the green belongs to the change and the reds are its, not the environment's.
item_verdicts.goal: section 23 asks that a dispatch launching its run returns that run id and never a scope-conflict naming the claim the same call just made; at the delivered head `_publish_launch_claim` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1069) writes the run's own claim at phase "starting" before the worktree step (dispatch.py:3938) and the post-publication read drops the caller's own identity (dispatch.py:4246), so the call can no longer refuse itself while a peer arriving inside the span meets the claim — the invisible-claim window the earlier incident ran over.
item_verdicts.manifest: read at /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/s22-coord/a-launch-is-not-its-own-conflict/manifest.md — the delivery record (both commits, both arms, the control and its plugin, the ruff delta, the introducing commits) is complete and every claim I checked held: base and head resolve with the subjects it states, my own base arm reproduces its two reds, and the control's log opens with the declared mutation verbatim and reddens the acceptance test with the dispatch refused by the claim of its own run id; the status field now reads in-progress because a later addition was received against this node and its checkpoint names it, so this review is scored against the delivered revision 3704ed56, never the tree's working files.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares five paths and the two commits touch exactly those five across 3be868de..3704ed56 (diff --stat: dispatch.py +107/-4, the new test module +342, the plan page's section +52, the evidence anchor +77, the figure +55), nothing outside the fence; the module itself asserts the real live-pointer directory carries no fixture pointer before and after every case, so the isolation is measured rather than assumed.

justifications.durability: the four cases falsify the defect in both directions — the invisible-claim window (red at base: observed [] against [first_run_id]) and the mid-launch peer claim that the base code missed at the pointer write (red at base: DID NOT RAISE), with the unwind case measured by readers shown to see a present run in the positive control, and the declared control forces the identity exclusion empty so the acceptance test reddens with a self-conflict; the residue is this review's finding (the published claim's pre-spawn shape is asserted nowhere) plus the pid-less hard-kill window no in-process test can cover.
justifications.evidence: the two-arm gate is recorded with the imported modules' paths printed per arm, the 84-test collect count has its own log, the declared control's first line is the mutation verbatim and its red arm is refused by the run's own run id, and I re-ran the added module in both pinned scratch trees myself (4 passed at head; 2 failed 2 passed at base); the figures I did not re-derive are the ruff format-hunk counts (6/6, read from the manifest) — the ruff check counts (7 base, 7 head) I measured myself and they agree.
justifications.fit: names are mechanism-named (`_publish_launch_claim`, `exclude_run_ids`) and the changed paths and added lines carry no plan, stage or ticket label (the repo's own naming greps over them return nothing), the docstrings state the mechanism and the reproduction rather than the task, the case names say what they demonstrate, and the composition reuses the existing pointer writer and claims read instead of adding a parallel path.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the deliverable is met end to end and independently reproduced — the claim is visible to a peer for the whole pre-spawn span, the identity exclusion removes the only self-refusal, and every refusal after publication unwinds the claim — with one deliberate judgement I checked rather than scored as a gap: a launch hard-killed between the publication and the full pointer write leaves a pid-less claim that claims.py (250-255) binds by design and `_observed_phase` (recovery.py:2747) reads as "nothing has happened yet", i.e. the conservative direction, while the base ordering left the same crash window holding the paths with no claim at all.
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path across 3be868de..3704ed56 lies inside the five the manifest declares, the code change carries nothing the goal does not imply (the exclusion parameter, the publication call and the unwind guard are what publishing before the worktree exists requires), and the three documentation paths are the landing contract's own deliverables rather than incidental edits.
